$schema_note: Hand-written artifact paired with examples/01_embed_and_compare.py and examples/figures/01_esm2_cosine_similarity.png. Schema is intentionally minimal until there is a second experiment to standardise against.

embedding.output: per-residue final hidden states, then mean-pooled across residues

metric.name: cosine_similarity
metric.definition: dot(a, b) / (norm(a) * norm(b)) on mean-pooled embeddings

observations: Hb alpha vs Hb beta (paralogs): 0.9781 — closer than either pair vs adenylate kinase.
The Hb-paralog cosine sits roughly 0.28 above the Hb-vs-AdK cosines.
what_this_shows: Off-the-shelf ESM-2 35M mean-pooled embeddings preserve enough signal to rank a paralog above an unrelated enzyme on three sequences.
The script asserts the ordering (Hb alpha-beta > Hb-AdK), not magnitudes.
what_this_does_not_show: It is not a fold-recognition benchmark. n = 3 sequences is far too small to claim anything about fold space.
Mean-pooling discards positional structure; per-residue or attention-aware probes may give very different rankings.
Cosine similarity in ESM-2 space is empirically squeezed into a narrow band; differences should not be interpreted as probabilities.
No comparison to TM-score, no comparison to baselines (random vectors, k-mer counts, BLOSUM), no error bars.
note: Values are taken directly from the script's reported output on first run (printed to stdout). They are exact to the precision shown; the script prints 4-decimal formatting. If a future rerun changes them due to library version drift, this file should be regenerated.
